subject: Clarification on default request/response log retention and prompts vs outputs
messages:
From: Security Team <security@acmecorp.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Sara Ong <sara.ong@finserve.io>
Date: 2027-09-14T10:05:00Z
Subject: Clarification: default retention for request/response logs

Hi Priyom,

We're doing a quick compliance review ahead of our procurement call next week and need to understand Redwood's default behavior around request/response logs. A few concrete questions:

- What is the default retention period for request/response logs (prompts and model outputs) on the hosted API?
- Do you treat prompts (customer inputs) differently from outputs (model-generated text) for retention and access?
- How are transient artifacts handled (KV cache/prefix cache) — are those persisted and, if so, for how long?
- If a customer issues a deletion request, what is the SLA for full removal from backups/analytics indexes?

We're primarily concerned about PII accidentally being retained in prompts and want to align on how long those items could persist. If you have a short diagram or SOC2 artifact you can share that would be ideal.

Thanks — happy to hop on a short call if it's easier.

—Security Team (AcmeCorp)
From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
To: Security Team <security@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Sara Ong <sara.ong@finserve.io>
Date: 2027-09-14T12:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Clarification: default retention for request/response logs

Hi — thanks for the clear list. TL;DR: hosted default is 30 days for request/response logs; prompts and outputs are retained together by default; Dedicated/Private customers can control retention. Details below and attaching a quick deletion-workflow diagram + SOC2 evidence matrix.

What we mean by terms:
- "Prompt" (input): the text and structured data sent by the customer (what you typed or the request payload).
- "Output" (response): tokens produced by the model plus any structured tool-call payloads.
- "Transient artifacts": KV cache, prefix caches, session-level caches used by the serving runtime to accelerate inference.

Hosted (Redwood API) — default behavior:
- Default retention: 30 days for request/response logs (this includes prompt and output together for debugging, quality, and tooling like reruns).
- Prompts vs outputs: both are treated as part of the request/response log. We do not split them into different default retention buckets unless a contractual change is requested.
- Transient artifacts: by default, runtime caches are ephemeral and not written to long-term object storage. KV/prefix cache entries live in in-memory stores and on-disk local caches for performance only; they are not part of the 30-day audit logs.
- Deletion requests: once an authorized deletion request is received, we kick off a staged purge: primary index and object store purge within 24–72 hours; analytics indexes and derived artifacts removed within 5 business days; backups are rotated/compacted and fully expire per backup TTL not exceeding 90 days unless otherwise contractually agreed.

Dedicated / Private deployments:
- For Dedicated (reserved capacity) customers we can set retention via configuration (e.g., 0/7/30/90 days) and include SLA terms in the contract.
- For Private (VPC/on-prem) the customer controls retention entirely; Redwood's control plane will not retain request/response logs unless explicitly configured.

PII & Redaction:
- Customers can enable client-side redaction before sending inputs to the API, or we offer a server-side redaction filter that strips or tokenizes common PII patterns prior to storage; enabling server-side redaction will remove the fields before the 30-day log write.

Notes on caching & reruns:
- Reruns and evals that use stored prompt sets are considered derived artifacts; these are tracked in the evaluation system and are subject to the same retention unless explicitly excluded.

Attachments: deletion_workflow.drawio (diagram of purge steps), soc2_evidence_matrix.xlsx (mapping of controls to artifacts). Also linking a draft KB page we plan to publish.

If you'd like, we can map this behavior to a short set of customer-facing bullet points for your procurement team. Happy to join a 20m call.

Best,
Priyom
Director, Product Security
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-14T16:10:00Z
Subject: FW: Clarification: default retention for request/response logs — confirm public wording

Priyom / Rishi — forwarding Acme's note and your reply. A couple quick follow-ups from legal/CS that came in:

- Legal: can we tighten the backup TTL language to a maximum of 90 days (rather than the more generic "not exceeding 90 days") and add a line that backups are immutable and only removed at rotation/expiry events?
- CS: wants a short customer-facing sentence that says: "By default, Redwood retains request and response logs for 30 days; customers can request deletion and enable server-side PII redaction."

Also linking the HubSpot record for FinServe so we can align messaging for that deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/99821

On the diagram: small nit — the purge step timestamp should show "24–72 hours" not "24–48" to match what Priyom wrote.

Marissa
Sr. Product Manager, Privacy & Controls
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-15T15:22:00Z
Subject: Re: FW: Clarification: default retention for request/response logs — confirm public wording

Thanks — quick decision to avoid blocking procurement:

- Final public line: "Redwood retains request and response logs (including prompts and model outputs) for 30 days by default. Customers may enable server-side PII redaction or request shorter/longer retention under contract."
- Backup language: update to: "Backups are retained for a maximum of 90 days and are purged on rotation/expiry events only; deletion requests will be applied to primary stores and derived artifacts as described above."
- Action items: Priyom to attach the updated deletion_workflow.drawio and SOC2 mapping to the KB draft; Marissa to publish the KB note and notify CS; I'll coordinate a one-pager for procurement.

I'll loop in Solutions Ops if FinServe pushes for any special retention SLA.

Rishi
Head of Trust & Safety
